During treatment with this medication, avoid consuming foods that may contain Listeria, such as deli meats, unpasteurized milk and cheese products, soft cheeses, and undercooked meat, seafood, or poultry. Alternatively, ensure these foods are thoroughly heated before consumption. 2. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It is crucial not to become pregnant while using alemtuzumab, as this medication can harm an unborn baby. 3. Your doctor will likely order a pregnancy test before starting this medication. Discuss reliable forms of birth control to use during treatment and for at least three months after the last dose. 4. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication and for at least three months after the last dose. 5. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 6. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. 7. Laboratory and medical tests, such as complete blood counts, kidney, liver, and thyroid function tests, and blood pressure monitoring, should be conducted before starting treatment, during treatment, and for some time after completing treatment. Attend all scheduled medical and lab appointments. 8. If you miss a dose, it is important to receive the medication as scheduled. Contact your healthcare provider for guidance. 9. This medication is administered via intravenous injection over two hours by a healthcare professional. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. 10. Before receiving this medication, your doctor may instruct you to take other medications, such as acetaminophen, diphenhydramine, corticosteroids, antibiotics, or antiviral medications, to help prevent side effects and infections. 11. Common side effects may include diarrhea, stomach or abdominal pain, fatigue, headache, tremors, difficulty sleeping, or mouth sores. Notify your doctor if these symptoms persist or worsen. 12. Serious side effects, though rare, may occur. These include blood disorders (e.g., decreased bone marrow function leading to low blood cell counts), infusion reactions, or a rare but potentially fatal brain infection called progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). Inform your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms such as fever, chills, flushing, dizziness, shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, or rash/itching. 13. Alemtuzumab may cause dizziness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit alcohol consumption, as it may exacerbate dizziness. 14. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using alemtuzumab before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations, as this medication may increase your risk of serious infections. 15. This medication increases the risk of a serious bacterial infection caused by Listeria. Avoid high-risk foods or ensure they are properly heated during and for some time after treatment. 16. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. This document is a summary and does not contain all possible information about the product. It does not replace professional medical advice.
